about.title: Banning Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Banning sits along the I-10 corridor, where distribution centers, trucking operations, and construction sites keep a steady flow of workers moving through the area. When someone gets hurt on the job here, the first step is usually a workers' compensation claim through the employer, since California treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy in most cases regardless of fault. But workplace injuries aren't always that simple. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on a road like W Ramsey Street contributed to the accident, a separate third-party injury claim may also be possible alongside workers' comp. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge any fee. We simply connect injured workers in Banning with an independent attorney who can look at the details of the incident, explain which path or paths apply, and help sort out reporting deadlines before they slip by.

whyChoose.title: Why Banning Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Untangle Workers' Comp From Third-Party Claims
items.desc: California generally limits an employee's recovery from their employer to workers' compensation, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be pursued separately. An attorney can help figure out which claims actually apply to your situation.

items.title: Deadlines Matter, Especially the 30-Day Window
items.desc: Reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days is required to protect your workers' comp rights, and a separate third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Missing either can close doors that would otherwise stay open.

items.title: Retaliation for Reporting Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers for reporting an on-the-job injury. An independent attorney can advise you on your rights if you feel pressured after speaking up.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work near the I-10 in Banning. Does workers' comp cover that?
items.answer: If you were performing job duties at the time, workers' compensation likely applies regardless of fault. However, if another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver. An attorney can review the specifics and explain how the two claims interact.

items.question: Can I still file a claim if my employer says the injury wasn't serious enough?
items.answer: Yes, the severity of the injury isn't up to your employer to decide. As long as you report it within 30 days, you have the right to pursue workers' compensation, and an attorney can help if your claim is disputed or delayed.

items.question: What if I'm afraid my employer will retaliate against me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal under California law. If you're worried about your job security after an injury on a Banning job site, an independent attorney can walk you through your protections before you report anything.
